entry.evidence: only few studies have investigated the palaeoceanographic evolution of the EGC in the northern part of the East Greenland shelf

steps.action: The authors set the aim of reconstructing EGC dynamics and variability off NE Greenland at centennial resolution through most of the Holocene.
steps.quote: we aim to reconstruct the dynamics and variability of the EGC off NE Greenland at centennial resolution throughout most of the Holocene

steps.action: They recovered gravity core 73G and a Rumohr core with an intact sediment-water interface from a depression on the mid-shelf, on the EGC flow path, with the site chosen from sub-bottom profiler data.
steps.quote: was collected on 16 September 2017 at 385 m water depth in an isolated bathymetrical depression on the NE Greenland shelf

steps.action: They measured a CTD temperature and salinity profile of the modern water column at the coring station before coring.
steps.quote: Temperature and salinity of the water column were measured in situ by a Seabird CTD

steps.action: They generated the proxy records: Itrax XRF scanning and radiographs, benthic and planktic foraminiferal counts at 5 cm (at least 300 benthic specimens), E. clavatum δ18O and δ13C, IRD weights and laser grain size.
steps.quote: The archive halves were scanned with an Itrax X-ray fluorescence (XRF) core scanner (Cox Analytical)

steps.action: They built an age-depth model from six AMS 14C dates, calibrated with Marine20 and ΔR = 0 ± 50 yr, using an OxCal P-sequence model extrapolated below the lowest date.
steps.quote: The age-depth model was made with the OxCal v4.4 software (Ramsey, 2008) using a P-sequence depositional model.

steps.action: They recalibrated the dates with Marine13 (ΔR = 150 ± 50 yr) and showed that the median ages differ by much less than the uncertainties.
steps.quote: for this specific Holocene reconstruction, the differences between using Marine13 and Marine20 are much smaller than the associated uncertainties

steps.action: They corrected the chronology for 12 cm of top loss by XRF correlation with the Rumohr core, and restricted the dated record to the last 9.4 kyr because the bottom 65 cm contains reworked Plio-Pleistocene fauna and has no dates.
steps.quote: indicated that 12 cm sediment was missing from the top of core 73G

steps.action: They described the XRF element trends, the foraminiferal assemblages divided into five visually defined ecozones, and the stable isotope series (three samples rejected, outliers at 140 cm kept).
steps.quote: These zones were defined by visual evaluation and interpretation of the species abundances.

steps.action: They compared the modern CTD bottom-water properties with published Westwind Trough and Norske Trough waters and inferred that cool AAW, not RAW, is the present Atlantic-sourced water at the site.
steps.quote: closer in character to the water found in the Westwind Trough than that of the Atlantic-sourced water presently seen in the Norske Trough

steps.action: They grouped indicator species (Atlantic Water, chilled Atlantic Water, Arctic Water, sea-ice edge, and agglutinated taxa) by environmental preferences taken from published modern-distribution studies, which gives the proxy-to-water-mass model.
steps.quote: we place selected benthic calcareous foraminiferal species into groups that are based on environmental preferences of the species

steps.action: They proposed that the mixed in situ and reworked Plio-Pleistocene fauna in the bottom 65 cm records glacier breakup and retreat before 9.4 ka, and left the question to further study.
steps.quote: we here suggest that the breakup and significant retreat of a nearby glacier caused reworking of older sediments

steps.action: From S. horvathi together with Atlantic indicators, and from concentrations and Ca/Fe, they inferred a highly stratified, sea-ice-loaded early Holocene water column with strong Atlantic subsurface inflow, high productivity, and the Polar Front nearby.
steps.quote: This combination of Atlantic-sourced bottom water and sea ice suggest a highly stratified water column in the Early Holocene

steps.action: They stated rival explanations for the low δ18O (Greenland Ice Sheet meltwater versus warmer bottom water) and tentatively linked the 8.5-8.4 ka terrigenous XRF peak to iceberg release during the 8.2 ka event.
steps.quote: Alternatively, the low δ 18 O values seen here may be a consequence of the warmer bottom waters.

steps.action: They compared the early Holocene reconstruction with PS93/025 (Syring 2020a, Zehnich 2020), the SE Greenland cores (Jennings 2011) and JM10-330 (Consolaro 2018) and found agreement.
steps.quote: Our suggestions of cold water and sea ice at the surface combined with Atlantic-sourced bottom waters is in accordance with recent reconstructions

steps.action: Using cool Fram Strait deep water at JM10-330 as evidence of a weak RAC, they attributed the early Holocene subsurface Atlantic influx to AAW rather than the RAC.
steps.quote: point to a weakened RAC, suggesting that the strong water column stratification on the NE Greenland shelf was due to increased AAW influx

steps.action: They explained the early Holocene stratification by extensive Greenland Ice Sheet melt, and the weak 8.2 ka signal by a persistent fresh surface layer, drawing on cited deglaciation and model studies.
steps.quote: can be explained as a consequence of the extensive melting of the Greenland Ice Sheet

steps.action: From peak C. neoteretis, P. bulloides and A. glomerata and the near absence of sea-ice taxa, they inferred the warmest bottom waters (an HTM, 8.2-6.2 ka) driven by a strengthened RAC, with the Polar Front moving away from the site.
steps.quote: We suggest that this may be explained by a strengthening of the RAC, transporting RAW to our site

steps.action: They set the HTM reconstruction against Fram Strait, East Greenland and Nordic Seas records showing strong AW flow and warm conditions until about 7-6 ka.
steps.quote: This is supported by several studies from the Fram Strait

steps.action: From the return of S. horvathi and the decline of C. neoteretis, they inferred renewed stratification with sea-ice-loaded surface water and weaker but persistent Atlantic subsurface inflow between 6.2 and 4.2 ka.
steps.quote: This suggests a return to a more stratified water column with sea-ice-loaded surface water and Atlantic-sourced subsurface waters.

steps.action: They compared the 6.2-4.2 ka interval with records of a weakening RAC, cooling, sea-ice expansion and ice-margin advance from the Fram Strait, PS93/025, Iceland and the ice margin.
steps.quote: Similar to our record, a sediment core retrieved north of our location

steps.action: From S. feylingi, cold-water agglutinated taxa, minimal terrigenous elements and heavier δ18O, they inferred a change at 4.2 ka to increased Polar Water, reduced RAW, freshening and (near) perennial sea ice.
steps.quote: Our record shows clear evidence of significant changes occurring at 4.2 ka.

steps.action: Using the foraminiferal fauna, they rejected bottom-water warming as the cause of the light δ18O spike in favour of brine rejection, and found no short-lived 4.2 ka event excursion.
steps.quote: cannot be attributed to sudden bottom-water warming on the basis of the foraminiferal fauna

steps.action: They compared the 4.2-3.2 ka reconstruction with records of reduced AW transport and strengthened EGC from the Fram Strait, PS93/025, the central Greenland shelf and the Denmark Strait.
steps.quote: Harsh conditions and strengthened EGC with permanent sea-ice cover dominated the central Greenland shelf as well

steps.action: From S. feylingi, S. difflugiformis, rising δ13C and chilled-AW taxa, they inferred a Neoglacial strengthened EGC with thick Polar Water and AAW subsurface inflow from 3.2 ka.
steps.quote: The results point to cold and unstable conditions with minimum surface-water productivity and increasing sea-ice cover at our location.

steps.action: They compared the Neoglacial interval with late Holocene cooling records (West Spitsbergen, Greenland Sea, West Greenland, Iceland) and with the Renssen et al. (2006) model mechanism.
steps.quote: a general cooling trend has been reported, with more severe sea-ice conditions

steps.action: They proposed that the varying RAW/AAW and Polar Water proportions covary with northward heat transport, and associated the post-HTM cooling with a shift towards a more negative NAO/AO and with later impacts on the Subpolar Gyre and the AMOC.
steps.quote: We therefore associate the gradual cooling trend seen in our record as well as at other North Atlantic sites with a continuous transition

steps.action: They kept the multiproxy reconstruction of EGC strength, water masses, sea ice and productivity over the last 9.4 kyr as the paper's conclusion.
steps.quote: allowed us to reconstruct changes in sea surface productivity, subsurface-water temperatures, sea-ice conditions, Greenland Ice Sheet melting, and the strength of the EGC

end.claim: Over the last 9.4 kyr the NE Greenland shelf moved from a stratified, sea-ice-loaded early Holocene with strong Atlantic subsurface inflow, through an RAC-dominated HTM (8.2-6.2 ka), to a strengthened, fresher EGC with more Polar Water after 4.2 ka and especially after 3.2 ka.

decisive_move.sentence: Assigning benthic foraminiferal species to water-mass and sea-ice groups from their published environmental preferences is what turns the assemblage counts into the water-mass reconstruction.

gates.evidence: The core was taken for its position on the EGC flow path (§2 ¶1, §3 ¶1); no hypothesis directed the acquisition. Interpretations were checked against independent proxies in the same core (Ca/Fe; foraminifera for the δ18O spike; foraminifera failing to show the 8.2 ka signal) and against other cores, but no prediction was stated beforehand. Ecozones were defined visually after the data were seen (§4.4.2 ¶6).

imports.item: Bayesian P-sequence deposition model in OxCal
MAT253 isotope ratio mass spectrometer with Kiel IV carbonate device
Environmental preferences of modern benthic foraminiferal species

novelty_claims.quote: The reconstruction provides new insights into the not yet resolved palaeoceanographic evolution of this region

limits: No review file or discussion version was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The paper does not report how the site, sampling interval, or indicator species were chosen beyond location and preferences cited from the literature. Ecozone boundaries were set visually, with no statistical zonation or counting-error estimates. The reconstruction rests on a single core, and ΔR = 0 ± 50 yr is assumed without local justification beyond cited practice. The chronology of the bottom 65 cm is unresolved. Rival explanations are mostly left open or decided by qualitative appeal to other proxies or cited records; there is no formal test. Sub-claims at other statuses: the age model is an estimate_with_resolution (2-sigma ranges, Table 1); the link of the 8.4 ka XRF peak to the 8.2 ka event is a weak best_explanation (seen in one proxy only); the NAO/AO mechanism and the Subpolar Gyre/AMOC implications are speculative best_explanation claims resting on cited work; the glacier-retreat origin of the reworked basal section is a hypothesis flagged as needing further study. Inference: the walk is descriptive-interpretive, with comparison to regional records acting as the main check.

disagreements.target: Heaton et al. (2020) statement that Marine20 is not suitable for polar regions
disagreements.support: The authors argue that the same limitation applied to the widely used Marine13, that Marine20 is now widely used in the Arctic, and that Marine13 and Marine20 ages differ by less than the uncertainties (Table A1).
disagreements.quote: We are aware that Heaton et al. (2020) state that the Marine20 is not suitable for polar regions.

disagreements.target: The 8.2 ka cold event as recorded in Greenland and northern North Atlantic archives (e.g. Risebrobakken et al., 2003; Ellison [...]
disagreements.support: Only a short XRF terrigenous peak appears at the site, with no foraminiferal or isotope response, which the authors explain by a persistent fresh surface layer, as at other EGC-influenced sites.
disagreements.quote: The strong freshwater discharge might have also weakened the recording of the 8.2 ka cooling event at our location

disagreements.support: Apart from a single A. glomerata sample, the record shows only a general environmental change at 4.2 ka, not a short-lived excursion.
disagreements.quote: there is no evidence of a shorter-lived climate excursion that might be linked to the so-called 4.2 ka event (Weiss, 2017)

alternatives_considered.reason: Marine13 has the same polar limitation; Marine20 is widely used in the Arctic; differences are smaller than the uncertainties

alternatives_considered.chosen: Relative abundances as a percentage of total benthic (calcareous plus agglutinated) fauna
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Separate percentages within the agglutinated and calcareous groups; absolute concentrations (ind. per g)
alternatives_considered.page: §3 ¶5; Figure A2; Figure A3; Figure A4; Figure A5

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Warmer RAW; presence due to wind-driven upwelling
alternatives_considered.reason: CTD bottom-water temperature and salinity resemble Westwind Trough water

Increased AAW influx as the cause of early Holocene stratification

alternatives_considered.reason: Cool deep-water conditions in the eastern Fram Strait (Consolaro et al., 2018) point to a weakened RAC

alternatives_considered.reason: The foraminiferal assemblage points to low bottom-water temperatures
